items.prose: Pouring soap batter into pine frame molds at heavy trace and bundling the molds in thick wool blankets trapped exothermic heat. The temperature climbed to 72°C, forcing the entire block through a translucent gel phase that locked in uniform saponification.

Demolding forty-eight hours post-pour, the fifty-kilogram soap block passed through a multi-strand piano wire harp. Tensioned 0.4mm spring-steel wires sliced the block cleanly into 300 crisp, rectangular 150-gram ration bars with zero crumbling.

Arranging cut bars on slatted red cedar racks under a steady 0.5 m/s dehumidified air draft cured the soap across six weeks. Moisture evaporated from 24% down to 11.8%, condensing the crystal lattice into an ultra-dense, long-lasting bar.

Exposure to moist, carbon-dioxide-rich bunker air during early curing formed a chalky white film of sodium carbonate efflorescence on bar tops. Passing the bars through a brief steam jet dissolved the ash bloom, restoring a glossy amber finish.

Formulating toilet soap with 6% superfatting left a small fraction of unreacted tallow, lanolin, and beeswax dispersed throughout the bar. The gentle emollient formula protected bunker personnel from harsh chemical dermatitis and eczema.

Dosing soap batter at trace with 1% steam-distilled pine needle oil infused the bars with natural alpha-pinene and limonene terpenes. The fragrant essential oils provided natural antimicrobial properties while completely masking raw tallow odors.

Shore A durometer penetration tests across fully cured fifty-day bars registered a hardness reading of 86. The rigid crystal matrix prevented bars from softening into mush when left in standing water trays in communal wash houses.
